content:
Yesterday we saw how jealousy hides behind another complaint, as it did with Miriam and Aaron. We ended with the piercing question that Yahweh asked them, a question that still searches every heart. Yahweh said, "Why were you not afraid to criticize my servant Moses?" (Numbers 12:8). That question should make us tremble. Before we speak about a brother, a sister, an elder, a servant, or a worker in the flock, we must first ask ourselves: Is this truth? Is this necessary? Is this done in love? Am I seeking restoration, or am I feeding bitterness? Am I speaking from genuine concern, or from jealousy?

When Yahweh judged Miriam, a visible sign came upon her body. Numbers 12:10 says, "There stood Miriam, her skin as white as snow from leprosy."

Her inward sin became outwardly visible. The jealousy that had been hidden in the heart became a public shame upon the body. Yahweh showed everyone that her words were not small in His sight. Now we must ask what visible sign may come upon us today. And here we must be careful, for we must not say that every sickness or trouble is caused by jealousy. Job suffered though he was righteous. Christ suffered though he was sinless. Many faithful servants pass through trials. But Scripture does show that Yahweh can chasten His people when they walk wrongly. Hebrews 12:6 says, "For the LORD disciplines those he loves, and he punishes each one he accepts as his child."

Sometimes the sign may be a loss of peace, for a bitter heart cannot rest. Sometimes it may be spiritual dryness, when prayer becomes distant, the Word becomes closed, and joy disappears. Sometimes the sign may be division around us, because bitterness spreads and troubles many. Sometimes Yahweh may allow our hidden attitude to be exposed before others. And sometimes, in serious cases, there may even be physical chastening, as Paul warned the Corinthians, "That is why many of you are weak and sick and some have even died" (1 Corinthians 11:30). Again, we must not judge every sickness as punishment, but neither must we ignore the warning that Yahweh can discipline His people seriously.

Miriam was also sent outside the camp for seven days. Numbers 12:14-15 tells us she was kept outside the camp for seven days, and the people waited until she was brought back before they traveled again. This is a fearful picture. The flock was moving forward under Yahweh's cloud, but Miriam had to stay outside for a time because of her sin. In the same way, if bitterness, jealousy, false accusation, or rebellion continues in us, we may find ourselves separated from the peace and fellowship of the flock that Christ is leading. Sometimes a believer may still attend the meetings, yet inwardly he is outside, cold, distant, offended, and unable to walk with joy. And in more serious cases, Scripture also speaks of church correction and separation for the purpose of repentance, for Paul wrote, "Remove the evil person from among you" (1 Corinthians 5:13). But even correction is never meant for destruction. It is meant to bring the person back. Miriam was not cast away forever. She was disciplined, humbled, and then restored. Yahweh's correction is serious, but it is also full of mercy when repentance comes.

Therefore, if jealousy or bitterness is in our hearts, today is the day to deal with it. Let us not wait until Yahweh exposes it. Let us not allow it to grow into criticism, accusation, division, or rebellion. Let us confess it while it is still hidden. Let us ask Yahweh to cleanse our hearts. 1 John 1:9 says, "But if we confess our sins to him, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all wickedness." If we have spoken against a brother or sister because of jealousy, let us make peace. If we have covered envy with spiritual language, let us be honest before Yahweh. If we have allowed bitterness to remain, let us pull it out today before it corrupts many.

Our Master said, "So if you are presenting a sacrifice at the altar in the Temple and you suddenly remember that someone has something against you, leave your sacrifice there at the altar. Go and be reconciled to that person" (Matthew 5:23-24). This is very practical. If jealousy has made us speak wrongly, we must not only pray privately. We must also make peace where peace is needed. A message may need to be sent. A phone call may need to be made. A confession may need to be spoken. A wound may need to be healed. A brother or sister may need to hear us say, "I was wrong." Paul says, "Indeed, the right time is now. Today is the day of salvation" (2 Corinthians 6:2). Today is the day to confess. Today is the day to remove bitterness. Today is the day to make peace. Today is the day to stop hiding jealousy behind another complaint.

Let us learn well from Miriam and Aaron. Yahweh blesses different members in different ways. One may be used to preach. One may be used to serve quietly. One may be given wisdom. One may be given hospitality. One may be given courage. One may be given prayerfulness. One may be given leadership. One may be given suffering through which others are strengthened. The body has many members, but one God works in all of them. 1 Corinthians 12:18 says, "But our bodies have many parts, and God has put each part just where he wants it." If Yahweh has placed a brother or sister in a certain service, let us not be jealous. Let us rejoice. Their blessing does not reduce our blessing.
Their calling does not cancel our calling. Their service does not make our service worthless.

So let us ask Yahweh for a clean heart. Let us honour His anointed ones. Let us speak carefully. Let us correct only in love, and never in bitterness. Let us rejoice when others are used by Yahweh. Let us remove jealousy before it becomes leprosy of the heart. Miriam's skin became white as snow, and the whole camp saw it. May Yahweh help us before our hidden bitterness ever becomes visible shame. May we confess today, forgive today, **make peace today, and return fully to the flock that Christ is leading. This completes our** study of Numbers chapter twelve. Yahweh willing, we will step into a new lesson tomorrow.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our Father,

Search our hearts and reveal any jealousy, bitterness, or selfish ambition hidden within us.

Forgive us for the times we have covered wrong motives with spiritual words.

Help us to rejoice when You bless our brothers and sisters.

Keep us from speaking against Your appointed servants.

Give us humility like Moses, repentance like Aaron, and restoration like Miriam.

Through Christ, cleanse our hearts and keep us walking with the flock.

"Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a loyal spirit within me." Psalm 51:10

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
